channel.title: Home Cooking Basics
channel.description: Kitchen fundamentals for people who want to cook with confidence.

item.title: Best By, Use By, Sell By, What Food Dates Actually Mean
item.description: USDA and FDA explain which food date labels are about quality, which one is legally required, and how to decide whether food past its date is still good.

item.title: How to Wash Fruits and Vegetables the Right Way
item.description: FDA's seven steps for cleaning fresh produce, why soap and produce washes are unnecessary, and why rinds you never eat still need a rinse.

item.title: Food Safety: How Long Leftovers Really Last
item.description: USDA guidance on the two-hour rule, safe refrigeration windows, and reheating temperatures that actually keep leftovers safe to eat.

item.title: Freezer Storage, How Long Food Actually Stays at Its Best
item.description: USDA's official freezer storage chart and refreezing rules, explaining the difference between food that's unsafe and food that's just past its best quality.

item.title: How to Scale a Recipe Up or Down Without Guessing
item.description: The actual math for resizing a recipe to more or fewer servings, using NIST's official measurement conversions, plus what does not scale linearly.

item.title: Safe Cooking Temperatures, What the Numbers Mean
item.description: USDA's official safe minimum internal temperature chart explained, including why rest time matters and why color is not a safety indicator.
